page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc6.10xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 40 dedicated physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a base frequency of 3.1 GHz. The instance is configured with 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.4 GB per core. It operates on the KVM hypervisor and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

Benchmark results place this instance consistently in the average performance tier. The Intel Xeon processor achieves a stress-ng single-core score of 1439.29 and a multi-core score of 38381.56. Memory performance is characterized by a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 2132.58 GB/sec, which drops to 105.52 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, alongside a write bandwidth of 36.66 GB/sec. In application-specific tests, the instance processes 34.66 million Redis SET operations per second and delivers a static web serving throughput of 23.2 GB/sec. For language model workloads, the system processes 1928.13 tokens per second for prompt processing on a small 135M model, declining to 57.07 tokens per second on a medium 7B model.

From a resource density perspective, the ecs.hfc6.10xlarge offers a high concentration of dedicated compute cores relative to its memory footprint. This makes it a cost-efficient option for CPU-bound tasks that do not require massive memory arrays or local NVMe storage. However, the absence of bundled local storage means users must provision external block storage, which may introduce latency and additional cost considerations. The instance is suited for workloads such as software compilation, multi-threaded decompression, static web serving, and database operations that benefit from dedicated physical cores and high clock speeds.
